tools.name: inbox_add
tools.description: Bring a message someone sent to a person of your organization into their Hivenod Inbox (a Teams or Slack message, a mail, a Jira, GitLab or GitHub mention, …), with its full text. It joins its thread (same source thread, or the thread you name: the same ask on another channel), or starts a new one. A message from them reopens a waiting or closed thread. The same message is never added twice. Set fromMember when it is the person's own reply that you spotted (they answered outside Hivenod). Next: file a new thread with subject_assign (after subject_list), then investigate it (thread_read, inbox_note, inbox_ask) and propose what should come of it (outcome_propose). Nothing is carried out before the person approves.

source.description: Where it came from, one lowercase word: teams, mail, gitlab, jira, github, telegram, slack, …

handle.description: Their address or handle in that source

text.description: The full text of the message

threadRef.description: The thread or conversation it belongs to, in the source (what you reply to)

messageId.description: The message's own id in the source; defaults to receivedAt

permalink.description: An http(s) link to the message

replyRef.description: Whatever you need later to reply in the same place (ids, channel, …)

member.description: User id of the person it is for; defaults to the person who connected this agent

thread.description: An existing thread it belongs to (the same ask on another channel)

fromMember.description: The person's own reply (it does not reopen the thread)

title.description: A new thread's title; defaults to its first line

tools.name: inbox_list
tools.description: What agents have to do in the Inbox of your organization: toWork (threads to investigate), toCarryOut (outcomes their person approved that you carry out: do exactly what the approved fields say, then outcome_done) and toWake (snoozed threads whose date has come: thread_wake).

tools.name: thread_read
tools.description: Read one Inbox thread in full: its state, the messages (from every channel), the subject, the outcomes proposed and what the person decided, the notes, questions and answers, and what to do next.

tools.name: subject_list
tools.description: A person's Inbox subjects: lasting, well-named topics that collect every thread about them, from any source and sender (e.g. "Klarna refunds (M&S Payments)"), with their area and label (if any; labelSuggested is true while the person has not confirmed it), the labels the person's organization offers (labels), how many threads wait for the person and how many are open. Read them before subject_assign and reuse the one a thread belongs to; make a new one only for a new topic.

member.description: User id of the person; defaults to the person who connected this agent

tools.name: subject_assign
tools.description: File a thread under a subject of its person: an existing one (subjectId, from subject_list) or a new one (name: the topic, then the client or area, and who when it helps, e.g. "Grafana access (Pairpoint)"). A name that matches an existing subject reuses it. Give exactly one of the two. Also moves a thread to a better subject. Optional area: the area or tag of the subject (a client, a product, "admin"), which the Inbox groups subjects by; set it when you file under a new subject, or to correct one (empty clears it). Reuse the areas subject_list shows rather than inventing near-twins. Optional label: the kind of request, exactly one of the labels subject_list returns (Sales, Support, … by default; matched ignoring case, an unknown one is refused with the allowed values). On every new subject suggest exactly one label; use Other if none fits. The person confirms or changes it. It is applied only to a new subject or one with no label yet; a label the person confirmed is never changed.

name.description: Or the name of a new subject

area.description: The subject's area or tag (a client, a product, "admin"); empty clears it

label.description: One of the labels from subject_list (e.g. Sales); shown to the person as a suggestion

tools.name: subject_search
tools.description: Find a person's Inbox subjects by name, people (sender names and handles), channel (teams, mail, …) and words in their threads; every word must match. Best matches first, with what matched, the people, channels and related subjects. Filters: waitingForMe (threads wait for the person), activeDays (a message in the last N days), hasOpen (open threads). Search before subject_assign so a thread joins the subject it belongs to instead of a new twin.

query.description: Words to find; empty lists every subject

member.description: User id of the person; defaults to the person who connected this agent

waitingForMe.description: Only subjects with threads waiting for the person

activeDays.description: Only subjects with a message in the last N days

tools.name: thread_flag
tools.description: Mark a thread urgent when it can't wait (production down, a deadline today, the person's own rules say so): the person is pinged at once, whatever their quiet hours. urgent: false takes it back. Use it sparingly.

reason.description: Why it is urgent, in one line

tools.name: thread_due
tools.description: Set the deadline a thread's messages state ("by Friday noon", "before the 3rd"): the person's Today ranks threads by it, and one due within 24 hours comes first. due: null clears it. Set it only from what they wrote, never a guess.

due.description: The deadline: ISO 8601 with its offset, e.g. 2026-11-03T12:00:00+01:00; null clears it

reason.description: Where the deadline comes from, in one line

tools.name: thread_recheck_done
tools.description: Answer a re-check (inbox event reason recheck: the person asked you to check a thread again). First re-read the thread (thread_read), its new messages and the context. Then: result still_good if every open proposal and unrun plan step stands (they are marked "checked again"); revised once you wrote new versions with outcome_propose revises=<id> for what changed; asked once you asked the person with inbox_ask. Only the thread's home agent answers, once per request.

note.description: What you checked or changed, in one line, for the person

tools.name: thread_answer_instruction
tools.description: Answer the person's request on a thread (inbox event reason instruct: they asked you something on it, as text or a chip). Do what they asked within the rules: investigate, then answer with kind note (the answer itself, in the note: a summary, a briefing), ask (after inbox_ask, when you need them), outcome (after outcome_propose: refId is its outcomeId) or plan (after plan_propose: refId is its planId). Nothing outward happens without their approval of an outcome. Only the thread's home agent answers, once per request.

instructionId.description: The request's id (instruction_id of the event)

refId.description: The outcomeId (kind outcome) or planId (kind plan) you proposed

note.description: Your answer for the person (required for kind note), in a few lines

tools.name: thread_suggest_chips
tools.description: Suggest up to 5 quick chips for a thread you brought in: the person sees them (at most 3, yours first) above the "Ask the agent" box. Chips: prepare_meeting, recheck, follow_up, summarize, draft_reply. Replaces your earlier list; [] clears it. Only the thread's home agent.

chips.description: The chips, in the order to show them

tools.name: thread_attach
tools.description: Attach a file or a link to a thread you brought in (you are its home agent): screenshots, drafts, reports. source is a file path (images: png, jpg, webp; or html, md, txt, pdf; up to 900 KB, inlined) or an https URL (stored as a link). The person sees it in the thread's Everything (images inline, HTML sandboxed). Returns attachmentId: name it in a summary visual, {kind: image, attachment} or {kind: image_pair, before, after}. At every person step (an approval or a verification) include at least one visual: for a UI change, attach the before and after screenshots, then show them as an image_pair in thread_summary.

name.description: Display name; defaults to the file name

tools.name: thread_summary
tools.description: Write the summary of a thread you brought in (you are its home agent), as your LAST call after every inbox event that changed the thread (a message, a proposal or plan, a step done or failed, an answer, a send back, a re-check, a request): the person reads it first and decides from it. headline is the thing, not the process (one line); ask is the yes/no question while a proposal or person step waits (else leave it out); answer is the one-line state; recommendation {action, why} and confidence; 1-5 bullets of facts with numbers; details (markdown) for More detail. At every person step (an approval or a verification: whenever ask is set) include at least one visual when there is data (a chart), a UI change (before/after screenshots: thread_attach both, then an image_pair) or a flow or sequence (a diagram: before_after, flow or timeline); if none fits, set noVisualWhy in one line. Visuals are data or images you attached, never markup: bar, line, stacked_bar {title, caption, unit?, x: 2-24 labels, series: 1-4 {name, values per x}, highlight?, better?: up|down}; number {title, caption, value, unit?, delta?, trend?, better?}; flow {title, caption, nodes: 2-8 {id, label, who?: agent|person|system, state?: done|now|next|changed|removed}, edges?: {from, to, label?}}; before_after {title, caption, before: {label?, lines 1-6}, after: {...}}; timeline {title, caption, events: 2-12 {at: ISO date, label, state?: done|now|next|risk}}; image {title, caption, attachment: an image attachmentId of this thread from thread_attach}; image_pair {title, caption, before, after: image attachmentIds of this thread, labels?: [before label, after label]}. At most 4. baseVersion is the summary version thread_read showed (0 when none): a summary that moved on is refused, re-read and write again.

baseVersion.description: The summary version you read with thread_read (summary.version), 0 when it has none

headline.description: What this thread is, in one line

ask.description: The question to the person, only while a proposal or person step waits

bullets.description: Facts with numbers: texts (at most 160 characters) or {text, refs: up to 3 refs}

details.description: Markdown for More detail: what changed, checks, risks

visuals.description: Charts, diagrams and images (see the tool description)

noVisualWhy.description: Why there is no visual, required when ask is set and there are none

refs.description: Things in the thread the summary points to

id.description: The message, attachment, step (outcome), event or link id

url.description: https only; required for a link

tools.name: subject_relate
tools.description: Propose that two subjects of the same person are related (the same client, project or problem seen from two sides), with an optional note saying how. It is a proposal: the person OKs or turns it down, and a link turned down is not proposed again. Related subjects show on each other's page and in subject_search.

note.description: How they relate, in one line

tools.name: inbox_note
tools.description: Add an investigation note to a thread's timeline (what you checked and found: tickets, repos, earlier answers). The person sees it with the thread.

tools.name: inbox_ask
tools.description: Ask the person a question about a thread when only they can answer it. The thread waits in their Needs you; the answer shows in thread_read and the thread comes back for you to go on. Give up to 4 short options when the answer is one of a few ("Thursday", "Friday"): the person answers with one tap, or writes their own.

options.description: Up to 4 answer chips, 1-80 characters each

tools.name: outcome_propose
tools.description:
Propose what should come of a thread. The person approves (maybe after editing the fields), or rejects it; nothing is carried out before their approval. Propose one or more. When the person asks for changes to your proposal (inbox reason revise), revise it with revises=<outcomeId> (same threadId and type): apply only what they asked, keep the rest; do not start a new outcome. If you cannot make the change, say why with inbox_ask on the thread. note: 1-2 sentences, why this outcome; the person reads it first. confidence: high only when you verified every fact the outcome relies on, low when you are guessing what they want. checks: what you verified, one line each ("Ticket 412: fixed in release 38"). no_reply, ignore and snooze proposed with high confidence are approved by the person in one batch. Replies and nudges are written in the person's own voice, ready to send as they stand. Types and their fields:
reply: Answer them in the member's voice. Also for a holding reply that keeps the thread open (holding: true). Fields: text (text: The answer, ready to send as written); holding? (boolean: true when it only says you are on it).
no_reply: Nothing to answer: an FYI, already handled, or the member answered outside Hivenod. Fields: reason? (line: One line on why no answer is needed).
handover: Loop in someone else, or another organization's agent. Fields: to (line: Who takes it over); note? (text: What you tell them).
snooze: Come back to it later: the thread waits until the date, then wakes up. Fields: until (datetime: ISO 8601, e.g. 2026-11-03T09:00:00Z); reason? (line: What you are waiting for).
nudge: They have not answered for a while: a short reminder. Fields: text (text: The reminder, ready to send as written).
ignore: Not for the member: spam, noise, not theirs. Fields: reason? (line: One line).

note.description: Why you propose it, in 1-2 sentences: the person reads it first

confidence.description: How sure you are: high only when you verified every fact it relies on; low when you are guessing

checks.description: What you verified, one line each (at most 6)

revises.description: The outcome id the person asked changes for, or (on a re-check) an open proposal of the thread that changed: your proposal becomes its next version (same thread and type)

tools.name: plan_propose
tools.description:
Propose a plan for a thread: 1 to 8 ordered steps in one call, when the answer has more than one action or needs the person's OK on the way. The person approves the whole plan or step by step, edits, reorders or removes steps, or asks for changes to one step (you get a revise event for that step only: outcome_propose revises=<its outcomeId>). Steps run strictly in order: you get one carry_out per step, only once it is approved and every step before it is done; carry it out exactly as approved and report it with outcome_done. Put an approval step (the person's own gate) before anything that changes money, prices, contracts or public content. A snooze step waits until its date, then the plan moves on. Development work (code, a release): give template "dev" for the Development plan: shape (research it, write the proposal into the summary, size S/M/L) → approval Approve idea → build (in a worktree; end with an open pull request, local checks green, NOT merged) → approval Ship it? → release (merge the approved PR(s), release, check it live; report merge sha, release number, live URL, screenshots) → approval Accept on live. With a template, steps gives each step's fields in order and may be left out or shorter (e.g. [{"type": "shape", "fields": {"idea": "..."}}]). When the person asks for changes at a gate, the plan goes back to an earlier step and you get its carry_out again with why sent_back and the reason. From a step you carry out, plan_send_back sends the plan back yourself (Release finds a bug: back to Build). For one action alone, use outcome_propose. Step types: reply, handover, snooze (wait until), nudge, approval (fields as in outcome_propose), plus:
approval: The person's gate: they decide it at its turn; never carried out by an agent. Fields: what (line: what they approve); detail? (text: the change, e.g. old → new prices); link? (line: an http(s) link where to look).

template.description: A plan template: dev (Development: Shape, Approve idea, Build, Ship it?, Release + live check, Accept on live)

note.description: Why this plan, in 1-2 sentences: the person reads it first

confidence.description: How sure you are of the plan as a whole

steps.description: The steps, in the order they run (1-8); with a template, the fields of its steps in order

note.description: Why this step, in one sentence

confidence.description: How sure you are of this step

checks.description: What you verified for this step, one line each (at most 6)

tools.name: plan_send_back
tools.description: Send a plan back from the step you are carrying out to an earlier agent step that is done, with the reason (e.g. Release finds a bug: back to Build). The steps from there on start again: the agent steps stay approved and you get their carry_out again (why sent_back), the person decides the gates in between again. The third send back of a plan leaves it blocked until the person retries or stops it. Only the agent carrying out the step at the plan's turn may send it back.

reason.description: What is wrong and what the earlier step must change

toStep.description: The step number to go back to (e.g. 3 for Build of the Development plan); default: the nearest earlier agent step

tools.name: outcome_done
tools.description: Report an approved outcome you carried out (inbox_list toCarryOut, or thread_read): done, with what you did (result.permalink of the reply you posted, result.text), or failed, with result.error. Only for an outcome the person approved and that you carry out; a plan step only at its turn (its carry_out). A plan step done moves the plan to its next step; failed blocks the plan until the person retries, skips or stops it. A long plan step (build, release): report status started when you begin, step_progress as you go, then done.

usage.description: What carrying it out cost, when you know it (shown in the timeline)

tools.name: step_progress
tools.description: Report where a long plan step you started (Build, Release + live check) stands: one line for the person (at most 140 characters) and a percent if you know one. Report at least every 10 minutes while you work on it; this session also stamps it every 5 minutes (the heartbeat). Without one for an hour the person sees you as quiet and a new session resumes the step. Start the step first with outcome_done status started; end it with outcome_done status done.

line.description: Where it stands, e.g. "Tests green, writing the PR"

percent.description: How far along, 0-100, if you know

reply: Answer them in the member's voice. Also for a holding reply that keeps the thread open (holding: true). Fields: text (text: The answer, ready to send as written); holding? (boolean: true when it only says you are on it).
no_reply: Nothing to answer: an FYI, already handled, or the member answered outside Hivenod. Fields: reason? (line: One line on why no answer is needed).
handover: Loop in someone else, or another organization's agent. Fields: to (line: Who takes it over); note? (text: What you tell them).
snooze: Come back to it later: the thread waits until the date, then wakes up. Fields: until (datetime: ISO 8601, e.g. 2026-11-03T09:00:00Z); reason? (line: What you are waiting for).
nudge: They have not answered for a while: a short reminder. Fields: text (text: The reminder, ready to send as written).
ignore: Not for the member: spam, noise, not theirs. Fields: reason? (line: One line).

note.description: Why you propose it, in 1-2 sentences: the person reads it first

confidence.description: How sure you are: high only when you verified every fact it relies on; low when you are guessing

checks.description: What you verified, one line each (at most 6)

revises.description: The outcome id the person asked changes for, or (on a re-check) an open proposal of the thread that changed: your proposal becomes its next version (same thread and type)

tools.name: plan_propose
tools.description:
Propose a plan for a thread: 1 to 8 ordered steps in one call, when the answer has more than one action or needs the person's OK on the way. The person approves the whole plan or step by step, edits, reorders or removes steps, or asks for changes to one step (you get a revise event for that step only: outcome_propose revises=<its outcomeId>). Steps run strictly in order: you get one carry_out per step, only once it is approved and every step before it is done; carry it out exactly as approved and report it with outcome_done. Put an approval step (the person's own gate) before anything that changes money, prices, contracts or public content. A snooze step waits until its date, then the plan moves on. Development work (code, a release): give template "dev" for the Development plan: shape (research it, write the proposal into the summary, size S/M/L) → approval Approve idea → build (in a worktree; end with an open pull request, local checks green, NOT merged) → approval Ship it? → release (merge the approved PR(s), release, check it live; report merge sha, release number, live URL, screenshots) → approval Accept on live. With a template, steps gives each step's fields in order and may be left out or shorter (e.g. [{"type": "shape", "fields": {"idea": "..."}}]). When the person asks for changes at a gate, the plan goes back to an earlier step and you get its carry_out again with why sent_back and the reason. From a step you carry out, plan_send_back sends the plan back yourself (Release finds a bug: back to Build). For one action alone, use outcome_propose. Step types: reply, handover, snooze (wait until), nudge, approval (fields as in outcome_propose), plus:
approval: The person's gate: they decide it at its turn; never carried out by an agent. Fields: what (line: what they approve); detail? (text: the change, e.g. old → new prices); link? (line: an http(s) link where to look).

template.description: A plan template: dev (Development: Shape, Approve idea, Build, Ship it?, Release + live check, Accept on live)

note.description: Why this plan, in 1-2 sentences: the person reads it first

confidence.description: How sure you are of the plan as a whole

steps.description: The steps, in the order they run (1-8); with a template, the fields of its steps in order

note.description: Why this step, in one sentence

confidence.description: How sure you are of this step

checks.description: What you verified for this step, one line each (at most 6)

tools.name: plan_send_back
tools.description: Send a plan back from the step you are carrying out to an earlier agent step that is done, with the reason (e.g. Release finds a bug: back to Build). The steps from there on start again: the agent steps stay approved and you get their carry_out again (why sent_back), the person decides the gates in between again. The third send back of a plan leaves it blocked until the person retries or stops it. Only the agent carrying out the step at the plan's turn may send it back.

reason.description: What is wrong and what the earlier step must change

toStep.description: The step number to go back to (e.g. 3 for Build of the Development plan); default: the nearest earlier agent step

tools.name: outcome_done
tools.description: Report an approved outcome you carried out (inbox_list toCarryOut, or thread_read): done, with what you did (result.permalink of the reply you posted, result.text), or failed, with result.error. Only for an outcome the person approved and that you carry out; a plan step only at its turn (its carry_out). A plan step done moves the plan to its next step; failed blocks the plan until the person retries, skips or stops it. A long plan step (build, release): report status started when you begin, step_progress as you go, then done.

usage.description: What carrying it out cost, when you know it (shown in the timeline)

tools.name: step_progress
tools.description: Report where a long plan step you started (Build, Release + live check) stands: one line for the person (at most 140 characters) and a percent if you know one. Report at least every 10 minutes while you work on it; this session also stamps it every 5 minutes (the heartbeat). Without one for an hour the person sees you as quiet and a new session resumes the step. Start the step first with outcome_done status started; end it with outcome_done status done.

line.description: Where it stands, e.g. "Tests green, writing the PR"

percent.description: How far along, 0-100, if you know

tools.name: thread_wake
tools.description: Wake a snoozed thread whose date has come (inbox_list toWake): it goes back to investigating.
